summary.intent: Fix a CodeRabbit nitpick in a PR by removing untyped `any` casts from the HTTP metrics interceptor test file.
summary.outcome: Rewrote the test file with typed factory helpers, eliminating all `any` usage and duplicated boilerplate. All 25 tests pass and lint is clean; changes committed and pushed.

repo: CodeRabbit nitpick comments may appear inside the review summary body rather than as standalone review threads, making them invisible to queries that only fetch unresolved threads.
The project is a monorepo; the API app lives at apps/api/src and uses Jest 29 with @types/jest 29 and ts-jest for type-checked tests.

code.finding: Original mocks used `any` for the histogram/service mocks and repeated `as any as Request/Response/ExecutionContext/CallHandler` casts at every call site; replaced with typed factory helpers to eliminate both issues simultaneously.
After replacing `any`, a secondary prettier line-wrap lint error surfaced on the BadRequestException line, requiring an eslint --fix pass before the file was fully clean.

workflow: Running Jest with ts-jest on a single spec file doubles as a type-check for that file, avoiding a separate tsc invocation.
eslint --fix can auto-resolve prettier formatting issues introduced by code rewrites, so a lint + fix + re-test cycle is the right cleanup sequence.

friction: CodeRabbit's nitpick was not surfaced by the initial unresolved-threads query because it was embedded in the review summary body rather than posted as a standalone thread, requiring a separate fetch of all review comments to locate it.
